from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Individual events are often unpredictable and chaotic.",
            "But groups of events follow strict, predictable patterns.",
            "This creates order from chaos, forming a bell curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: Order from Chaos", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1 in Yellow to match the Space Rabbits
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Show many yellow dots ('Space Rabbits') moving randomly
        num_dots = 45
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.07) for _ in range(num_dots)])
        
        # Get boundaries from grid system for initial distribution
        tl = self.grid["A1"]
        br = self.grid["D6"]
        
        for dot in dots:
            dot.move_to([
                np.random.uniform(tl[0], br[0]),
                np.random.uniform(br[1], tl[1]),
                0
            ])
        
        self.add(dots)
        
        # Define jitter movement using an updater for efficiency
        def jitter_dots(d, dt):
            # Move dots slightly in a random direction to simulate chaos
            d.shift(np.array([np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2), np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2), 0]))
            # Maintain dots within the upper grid area (A1-D6)
            if d.get_x() < tl[0]: d.set_x(tl[0])
            if d.get_x() > br[0]: d.set_x(br[0])
            if d.get_y() < br[1]: d.set_y(br[1])
            if d.get_y() > tl[1]: d.set_y(tl[1])

        for dot in dots:
            dot.add_updater(jitter_dots)
            
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset line 1 color and highlight line 2 in white
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # White horizontal axis appears at the bottom (Row F)
        axis = Line(self.grid["F1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["F6"] + RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(axis))
        
        # Dots stop jittering and move to form stacks
        # Using a binomial distribution (n=5, p=0.5) to simulate the Galton board outcome
        for dot in dots:
            dot.remove_updater(jitter_dots)
            
        bins = [[] for _ in range(6)]
        for dot in dots:
            bin_idx = np.random.binomial(5, 0.5)
            bins[bin_idx].append(dot)
            
        stack_anims = []
        for col_idx in range(6):
            col_key = str(col_idx + 1)
            base_pos = self.grid[f"F{col_key}"]
            for stack_idx, dot in enumerate(bins[col_idx]):
                # Stack dots vertically on the axis at each grid column
                target = base_pos + UP * (0.15 + stack_idx * 0.16)
                stack_anims.append(dot.animate.move_to(target))
                
        self.play(*stack_anims, run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reset line 2 and highlight line 3 in Cyan
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # A cyan bell curve outline fades in over the accumulated stacks
        # Center the curve based on the bin distribution (between col 3 and 4)
        center_x = (self.grid["F3"][0] + self.grid["F4"][0]) / 2
        baseline_y = self.grid["F1"][1]
        
        bell_curve = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 2.3 * np.exp(-((x - center_x)**2) / 1.5) + baseline_y,
            x_range=[self.grid["F1"][0]-0.3, self.grid["F6"][0]+0.3],
            color="#00FFFF"
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bell_curve))
        self.wait(4)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching lecture lines from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "A population represents the entire group we study.",
            "Samples are smaller subsets taken from that population.",
            "Distribution describes the shape and spread of data."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Knowledge: Population vs. Sample", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A large orange (#FF8C00) circle labeled 'Population' appears, filled with small cookie-shaped icons.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF8C00")
        
        pop_circle = Circle(radius=1.4, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(pop_circle, "A1", "D4")
        
        pop_label = Text("Population", color="#FF8C00", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(pop_label, "A2", scale_factor=0.8) 
        
        # Cookies inside population - using small brown dots
        cookies = VGroup()
        for _ in range(30):
            angle = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * PI)
            dist = np.random.uniform(0, 1.2)
            cookie_pos = pop_circle.get_center() + np.array([
                dist * np.cos(angle),
                dist * np.sin(angle),
                0
            ])
            cookie = Dot(point=cookie_pos, color="#D2691E", radius=0.06)
            cookies.add(cookie)
        
        self.play(Create(pop_circle), Write(pop_label), FadeIn(cookies))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A green (#00FF00) circle labeled 'Sample' appears as a small group of cookies moves into it.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        sample_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(sample_circle, "E5", "F6")
        
        sample_label = Text("Sample", color="#00FF00", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(sample_label, "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Select 6 cookies to move
        sample_indices = np.random.choice(len(cookies), 6, replace=False)
        sample_cookies_subset = VGroup(*[cookies[i] for i in sample_indices])
        
        self.play(Create(sample_circle), Write(sample_label))
        
        # Move cookies to sample circle area
        move_animations = []
        for i, cookie in enumerate(sample_cookies_subset):
            angle = np.random.uniform(0, 2 * PI)
            dist = np.random.uniform(0, 0.4)
            target_pos = sample_circle.get_center() + np.array([
                dist * np.cos(angle),
                dist * np.sin(angle),
                0
            ])
            move_animations.append(cookie.animate.move_to(target_pos))
            
        self.play(*move_animations)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # White (#FFFFFF) labels 'Mean = mu' and 'Mean = x-bar' appear next to the Population and Sample circles respectively.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Labels for means using MathTex for symbols
        mu_label = MathTex(r"\text{Mean } = \mu", color=WHITE, font_size=28)
        xbar_label = MathTex(r"\text{Mean } = \bar{x}", color=WHITE, font_size=28)
        
        self.place_at_grid(mu_label, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(xbar_label, "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(mu_label), FadeIn(xbar_label))

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        title = Text("The Central Limit Theorem (CLT)", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
        
        lecture_lines = [
            "1. Take samples from ANY distribution.",
            "2. Calculate the average of each sample.",
            "3. The distribution of these averages...",
            "4. ...will always be Normal (Bell Curve)!"
        ]
        
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=20).arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=LEFT) 
            for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5).shift(DOWN*0.5)

        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_vgroup, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # 2. Visual Representation Area (Right Side)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 2],
            y_range=[0, 1, 0.5],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 18}
        ).to_edge(RIGHT, buff=0.8).shift(UP*0.5)
        
        labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="Value", y_label="Prob")
        
        # Original Distribution: Uniform
        uniform_dist = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 if 1 <= x <= 9 else 0, color=YELLOW, x_range=[0, 10])
        dist_label = Text("Uniform Distribution", font_size=18, color=YELLOW).next_to(axes, DOWN)

        self.play(Create(axes), Write(labels))
        self.play(Create(uniform_dist), Write(dist_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Sampling Animation
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(axes.c2p(np.random.uniform(1, 9), 0.2), color=WHITE, radius=0.04) for _ in range(20)])
        sample_text = Text("Sampling...", font_size=18).next_to(dist_label, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Write(sample_text))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(dot) for dot in dots], lag_ratio=0.05))
        self.play(FadeOut(dots), FadeOut(uniform_dist), FadeOut(dist_label))

        # 4. Final Result: Normal Distribution
        # The CLT states that the distribution of means approaches a normal distribution
        mu = 5
        sigma = 1.2
        normal_dist = axes.plot(
            lambda x: (1 / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mu) / sigma)**2),
            color=GREEN,
            x_range=[0, 10]
        )
        result_label = Text("Distribution of Sample Means (Normal)", font_size=18, color=GREEN).next_to(axes, DOWN)

        self.play(Create(normal_dist), Write(result_label))
        self.play(Indicate(lecture_vgroup[-1], color=GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(title),
            FadeOut(lecture_vgroup),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(labels),
            FadeOut(normal_dist),
            FadeOut(result_label),
            FadeOut(sample_text)
        )

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Core Reveal: The Shape-Shifting Property", 
            [
                "Start with any population shape, even highly skewed ones.",
                "As sample size n increases, something magical happens.",
                "The distribution of sample means begins to shift shape.",
                "It always settles into a symmetrical normal distribution.",
                "This is the core of the Central Limit Theorem."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(PURPLE)
        
        # Shark Fin Population Shape
        shark_fin = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 4 * x * np.exp(-x),
            x_range=[0, 4],
            color=PURPLE
        )
        self.place_in_area(shark_fin, "A4", "B6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        pop_label = Text("Population", font_size=18, color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(pop_label, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(shark_fin), Write(pop_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        
        # Jagged Plot for small n=2
        # We create a manual jagged line that looks like a rough approximation
        jagged_points = [
            [-2, 0, 0], [-1.5, 0.2, 0], [-1, 0.8, 0], [-0.5, 0.4, 0], 
            [0, 1.2, 0], [0.5, 0.5, 0], [1, 0.9, 0], [1.5, 0.3, 0], [2, 0, 0]
        ]
        jagged_plot = VMobject(color=GRAY).set_points_as_corners([np.array(p) for p in jagged_points])
        self.place_in_area(jagged_plot, "D3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        n_label = Text("n = 2", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(n_label, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(jagged_plot), Write(n_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # n increases to 30
        n30_label = Text("n = 30", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(n30_label, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Slightly smoother but still somewhat jagged version
        medium_points = [
            [-2, 0, 0], [-1.2, 0.4, 0], [-0.6, 1.2, 0], [0, 1.5, 0], 
            [0.6, 1.2, 0], [1.2, 0.4, 0], [2, 0, 0]
        ]
        medium_plot = VMobject(color=GRAY_A).set_points_smoothly([np.array(p) for p in medium_points])
        self.place_in_area(medium_plot, "D3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Transform(n_label, n30_label), Transform(jagged_plot, medium_plot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Replaced CYAN with TEAL as CYAN is not a default constant in all Manim CE versions
        self.lecture[3].set_color(TEAL)
        
        # Smooth Bell Curve
        bell_curve = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 2 * np.exp(-x**2),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color=TEAL
        )
        self.place_in_area(bell_curve, "D3", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Transform(jagged_plot, bell_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        
        clt_text = Text("Central Limit Theorem", font_size=22, color=WHITE)
        normal_text = Text("Normal Distribution", font_size=22, color=GREEN)
        
        self.place_at_grid(clt_text, "C3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(normal_text, "F3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(clt_text), Write(normal_text))
        self.wait(2)

        )

        # Population Curve
        pop_curve = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: normal_pdf(x, 0, sigma_pop),
            x_range=[-3, 3, 0.05],
            color=COLOR_POP
        )
        # Using move_to with aligned_edge to keep it on the x-axis
        pop_curve.move_to([x_center, y_base, 0], aligned_edge=DOWN)

        # Sample Mean Curve (initially same as pop)
        sample_curve = pop_curve.copy().set_color(COLOR_SAMPLE)

        # Vertical dashed line at peaks
        peak_x = x_center
        peak_y_top = self.grid["A3"][1] + 0.5
        peak_y_bottom = y_base
        
        center_line = DashedLine(
            start=[peak_x, peak_y_bottom, 0],
            end=[peak_x, peak_y_top, 0],
            color=COLOR_TEXT
        )
        mu_label = MathTex(r"\mu", color=COLOR_TEXT, font_size=32)
        mu_label.next_to(center_line, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.add(x_axis)
        self.play(Create(pop_curve), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(sample_curve), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(center_line), Write(mu_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SAMPLE)
        
        # n label
        n_label_text = Text("n = ", font_size=24, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        n_value = DecimalNumber(1, num_decimal_places=0, color=COLOR_TEXT, font_size=24)
        n_group = VGroup(n_label_text, n_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(n_group, "B5")

        n_value.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(n_tracker.get_value()))
        
        # Updater for cyan curve
        def update_sample_curve(mob):
            n_val = n_tracker.get_value()
            if n_val < 1: n_val = 1
            sigma_sample = sigma_pop / np.sqrt(n_val)
            # Limit precision/height to prevent performance hit and off-screen peaks
            # Max height at sigma=0.1 is ~4.0, which fits in our grid
            new_mob = FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: normal_pdf(x, 0, sigma_sample),
                x_range=[-3, 3, 0.02],
                color=COLOR_SAMPLE
            )
            new_mob.move_to([x_center, y_base, 0], aligned_edge=DOWN)
            mob.become(new_mob)

        sample_curve.add_updater(update_sample_curve)
        
        self.add(n_group)
        self.play(n_tracker.animate.set_value(16), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_SAMPLE)
        
        # Indicator for width (Standard Error)
        def get_se_arrow():
            n_val = n_tracker.get_value()
            sigma_se = sigma_pop / np.sqrt(n_val)
            y_pos = y_base + 0.3
            # Arrow representing 1 sigma (Standard Error)
            arrow = DoubleArrow(
                start=[x_center, y_pos, 0],
                end=[x_center + sigma_se, y_pos, 0],
                buff=0,
                color=COLOR_TEXT,
                stroke_width=2,
                max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.2
            )
            return arrow

        se_arrow = always_redraw(get_se_arrow)
        se_text = Text("Standard Error", font_size=18, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        # Using updater for text position to follow the arrow
        se_text.add_updater(lambda t: t.next_to(se_arrow, UP, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(Create(se_arrow), Write(se_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_FORMULA)
        
        formula = MathTex(
            r"SE = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}",
            color=COLOR_FORMULA,
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2")
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_TEXT)
        
        # Show higher precision with even larger n
        self.play(
            n_tracker.animate.set_value(81),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Real-World Application: Why It Matters",
            [
                "The CLT is the powerhouse of modern statistics.",
                "We can study any population using normal distribution math.",
                "This allows for accurate predictions from small samples."
            ]
        )
        
        KHAKI = "#F0E68C"
        CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        GREEN = "#00FF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a khaki (#F0E68C) box representing '1 Million Lightbulbs'.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(KHAKI)
        
        large_box = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=2, color=KHAKI, fill_opacity=0.2)
        box_label = Text("1 Million Lightbulbs", font_size=18, color=KHAKI)
        
        # Place box in upper-center-right area
        self.place_in_area(large_box, 'B1', 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(box_label, 'A2')
        
        # Add many small dots inside the box to represent bulbs
        np.random.seed(42)
        bulbs_in_box = VGroup(*[
            Dot(point=large_box.get_center() + np.array([
                np.random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0),
                np.random.uniform(-0.8, 0.8),
                0
            ]), radius=0.03, color=KHAKI)
            for _ in range(100)
        ])

        self.play(
            Create(large_box),
            Write(box_label),
            FadeIn(bulbs_in_box)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Pull out a small cluster of 50 bulbs and draw a cyan (#00FFFF) bell curve over them.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(CYAN)
        
        # Create a small cluster
        sample_group = VGroup()
        for _ in range(50):
            dot = Dot(radius=0.03, color=KHAKI)
            sample_group.add(dot)
        sample_group.arrange_in_grid(rows=5, cols=10, buff=0.05)
        
        # Move sample group to area E4 to F6
        self.place_in_area(sample_group, 'E4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        sample_label = Text("Sample: 50 Bulbs", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(sample_label, 'D5')

        # Normal distribution curve (bell curve)
        ax = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3],
            y_range=[0, 1],
            x_length=2,
            y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "include_ticks": False}
        ).set_color(CYAN)
        
        curve = ax.plot(
            lambda x: np.exp(-x**2),
            color=CYAN
        )
        bell_curve_group = VGroup(ax, curve)
        self.place_in_area(bell_curve_group, 'E4', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Animation: Pulling bulbs from the box to the sample area
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(bulbs_in_box[:10].copy(), sample_group),
            Write(sample_label)
        )
        self.play(Create(bell_curve_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A green (#00FF00) arrow labeled 'Inference' points from the small curve back to the large box.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        inference_arrow = Arrow(
            start=self.grid['D5'],
            end=self.grid['D2'],
            color=GREEN,
            buff=0.1
        )
        inference_label = Text("Inference", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        # Position label near the middle of the arrow
        inference_label.next_to(inference_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(inference_arrow),
            Write(inference_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Clean up colors
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Averages: Demystifying the Central Limit Theorem
outline.target_audience: University students (Introductory Statistics) or high-level high school students

sections.title: The Hook: Order from Chaos
sections.content: Introduce the paradoxical idea that while individual events are unpredictable, the average of those events follows a strict, predictable pattern. Use a visual metaphor of a 'Galton Board' (Quincunx) to show randomness turning into a Bell Curve.
sections.example: Imagine thousands of tiny digital 'Space Rabbits' hopping randomly left or right. Individually, we can't guess where one rabbit lands. But when we look at the average position of groups of rabbits, a perfect 'Bell Shape' always emerges.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Population vs. Sample
sections.content: Establish the foundational vocabulary. Define the 'Population' (the entire group) and 'Samples' (small subsets). Explain the concept of 'Mean' (average) and 'Distribution' (the shape of the data).
sections.example: Visualize a 'Cookie Factory' with a giant vat of dough (Population). The individual cookies we bake are 'Samples.' Some cookies might have 5 chocolate chips, others 15, creating a 'Distribution' of chip counts.

sections.title: The Experiment: The Sampling Process
sections.content: Demonstrate the core mechanic of the CLT: 1. Take a random sample of size 'n'. 2. Calculate its mean. 3. Repeat this 1,000 times. 4. Plot the distribution of those 1,000 means. Emphasize that we are graphing the 'Average of Averages'.
sections.example: A robot named 'Data-Bot' picks 30 cookies at random, calculates their average weight, and marks it on a graph. Data-Bot repeats this process 500 times. The resulting graph is the 'Sampling Distribution of the Sample Mean'.

sections.title: The Core Reveal: The Shape-Shifting Property
sections.content: The most critical point: Regardless of the original population's shape (skewed, uniform, or weird), the distribution of sample means will always become a Normal Distribution (Bell Curve) as the sample size 'n' increases (usually n ≥ 30).
sections.example: Show a population distribution shaped like a 'Shark Fin' (highly skewed). As Data-Bot increases the sample size from n=2 to n=30, watch the 'Shark Fin' morph into a smooth, symmetrical 'Bell Curve' on the animation screen.

sections.title: Mathematical Nuance: Mean and Standard Error
sections.content: Introduce the properties of this new Bell Curve: 1. Its center (mean) is the same as the original population mean. 2. It becomes narrower (more precise) as the sample size 'n' increases. Introduce the formula for Standard Error: σ/√n.
sections.example: If the average weight of all cookies in the factory is 50g, the center of our Bell Curve will be exactly at 50g. If we sample 100 cookies instead of 10, the 'Bell' becomes much skinnier and taller, showing higher precision.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Why It Matters
sections.content: Explain that the CLT is the 'Powerhouse of Statistics' because it allows us to make inferences about any population using Normal Distribution math, even if the population itself isn't normal.
sections.example: An engineer tests 50 lightbulbs from a batch of 1 million. Because of the CLT, she can use the Bell Curve to calculate the exact probability that the entire batch meets quality standards without testing every single bulb.
